20531-up-to-date-business-including-less:
Up-to-Date Business, published in 1897, is a textbook of commerce for students entering trade and office work. Its lessons include banking and exchange, the machinery by which money moves between firms and countries. The book opens by sorting out its basic terms.

There is a distinction, it says, between the names commerce and business. Commerce is the interchange of products and goods between countries, or between different sections of the same country. Business covers the local work of buying and selling. On those definitions the lessons build, step by step, toward real office practice.

last-of-the-great-scouts-the-life-story-:
Helen Cody Wetmore told the life story of her brother, William F. Cody. The world knew him as Buffalo Bill. She dedicated the book to their mother's memory.

A family genealogy opens the volume, compiled in 1897. It claims descent from Milesius, an old Irish king. The story then follows Cody from boyhood to fame as a scout. Wetmore writes as a sister, with family knowledge and pride. Her book preserves the scout's legend as his own family wished it told. Cody's fame as a showman rests on the scout years told here. Family pride shapes which episodes receive most warmth.
podcast-dannyjones-uQXUNJgtBBU:
Movement coach Ido Portal joins Danny Jones to talk about an ancient tool he says can unlock human power. The episode title quotes his line on the work: it changes you. Portal is a trainer known for fluid, full body movement.

Portal explains his method, which treats the body as one linked system to be trained as a whole. He argues most gym work makes strong parts and a weak whole. Jones asks what proof backs the bold claims. Listeners who train will find a fresh lens on strength and skill. The library files the talk as an archive record.
podcast-joerogan-n8yZpKsaSbU:
Marcus Aurelius, the Roman emperor who wrote the Stoic classic Meditations, anchors this Joe Rogan Experience segment. Rogan and his guest look back at Aurelius and other ancient thinkers. The focus is what very old philosophy can still say to people now.

They talk through Stoic habits like facing hardship calmly and focusing on what you can control. The guest explains how Aurelius wrote his notes to himself while running an empire at war. Rogan connects the ideas to training, fighting, and daily stress. It is a plain-spoken intro to Stoic thought through the man who lived it at the top.
podcast-joerogan-qFwiXyZHYbU:
Dr. Robert Malone, a physician and researcher who worked on mRNA technology early in his career, talks with Joe Rogan in episode 2454. Malone became a leading critic of COVID policy and of the vaccines built on that platform. His Rogan visits draw huge audiences and sharp pushback.

Malone lays out his case against the pandemic response, from mandates to how health agencies handled risk data. He explains why he questions the safety reviews behind the shots. Rogan asks how a man from inside the field ended up outside it. The talk captures a central voice of the COVID dissent movement.
